newsitem.title: UK: Physical copper trade rejects hidden stock reports.
newsitem.headline: Physical copper trade rejects hidden stock reports.

text.p: Physical copper traders based in Europe dismissed recent reports of huge unreported copper stocks of as much as 600,000 tonnes lying in the Netherlands.

Last week the World Bureau of Metal Statistics (WBMS) said between 1990 and 1995 receipts of refined copper into bonded warehouses in the Netherlands had exceeded deliveries out by more than 500,000 tonnes.
"If we look at the numbers around 600,000 tonnes of copper appears to have gone into warehouses and not come out," Lloyd Davies, WBMS general manager said.
But traders said stocks on this scale could not go unreported for such a long time.
"I've been in this market for nearly thirty years and I know there couldn't have been this copper stored in Rotterdam," said one major merchant.
"If this material exists then let's see it," a trader added.

"The possibility of this stockpile existing is zero," said a third. "The only explanation I can give is that counting material going in and out of the Netherlands does not reflect material moving within the EEC," he added.
Traders said some copper may be held in bonded warehouses around the world, but tonnages were likely to be small.

Some said China may have a small amount of copper to re-export into London Metal Exchange (LME) warehouses in Singapore, but that is likely to be limited by stronger buying than expected from the Chinese state reserve.
"I understand that they (China's state reserve) have custom cleared most of the material that has gone out there," said one trader, estimating the total at 200,000 to 250,000 tonnes.
Traders and analysts agreed that copper stocks wordlwide did appear to be at or below the critically low level which they pegged at 3.5 to 4.0 weeks' consumption.
The impact on prices could be significant.
"You've got to be careful of copper. It could get explosive," one trader warned.
